---
format:
  typst:
    font-paths: resources/fonts
execute:
  warning: false
  echo: false
  message: false
  eval: true
---

```{=typst}
#set document(title: "Pingfan Hu - Resume", author: "Pingfan Hu")
// === PAGE ===
#set page(
  paper: "a4",
  fill: rgb("#F8F7F0"),
  margin: (top: 0.5in, bottom: 0.5in, left: 0.6in, right: 0.6in),
  footer: context {
    set text(size: 8pt, fill: rgb("#666"), style: "italic")
    let updated = datetime.today().display(
      "Updated [month repr:long] [day padding:none], [year]"
    )
    // one page, so no page count
    grid(
      columns: (1fr, 1fr),
      align(left)[#updated],
      align(right)[#link("https://pingfan.org")[pingfan.org]],
    )
  },
)

#set text(font: ("Optima", "Helvetica Neue", "Arial"), size: 10pt)

// === SPACING ===
// The CV's five gaps, at the resume's own sizes (it must fit one page).
// Every vertical gap in the document is one of them, used by name below;
// nothing adds space by hand.
//   line-gap     between the lines of a paragraph, a bullet or a table (the
//                leading), and between a head and what it heads
//   para-gap     between bullets and between blocks (here a line's gap: on
//                one page there is no room for a visible break, so the
//                heads carry the grouping)
//   head-gap     above an entry's title, and below a section head's rule
//   section-gap  above a section head
//   rule-gap     between a head's words and its rule
// A block asks for a paragraph's gap below it and only a line's above, so
// the gap after anything is the one it asks for, and a head asks for more
// room above. Typst collapses two neighboring gaps to the larger, so an
// entry right under a section's rule would take head-gap whatever the rule
// asked; every rule asks for it, so the space under a rule is one size.
// The page is full to within a few points: after a change, check
// `pdfinfo _site/resume.pdf` still says one page.
#let line-gap = 0.5em
#let para-gap = 0.5em
#let head-gap = 0.89em
#let section-gap = 1.23em
#let rule-gap = 0.4em
#set par(leading: line-gap, spacing: para-gap, justify: false)
#set block(above: line-gap, below: para-gap)

// === LISTS ===
// a bullet is a short gray hairline, a number gray Maple Mono with its
// period, as on the site
#let list-mark = box(height: 0.66em, width: 0.5em, place(horizon, line(length: 0.5em, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#A3A096"))))
#let enum-mark(n) = text(font: "Maple Mono NF", size: 0.8em, fill: rgb("#77746B"))[#n.]
#set list(indent: 1em, body-indent: 0.4em, marker: list-mark, spacing: para-gap)

// Navy-blue links
#show link: set text(fill: rgb(0%, 20%, 60%))

// === HELPERS ===
// A mark from the site's glyph map (resources/styles/styles.scss), read at
// compile time so the documents and the page share one drawing: gray, at
// the size of the text, its center 0.29em above the baseline, between the
// lowercase and capital centers, as the page's marks and the skill marks.
#let glyph(name, size: 0.9em) = {
  let scss = read("resources/styles/styles.scss")
  let svg = scss.match(regex("\n  \"" + name + "\": \"(<svg[^\"]*</svg>)\"")).captures.at(0)
  box(width: size, height: 0.58em, place(horizon + center, image(bytes(svg.replace("'black'", "'#77746B'")), height: size)))
}

// Section header with underline rule.
#let hair = rgb("#BDBAB0")
#let muted = rgb("#77746B")
#let section(name) = block(sticky: true, above: section-gap, below: head-gap, stack(spacing: rule-gap,
  text(size: 11pt, weight: "bold", tracking: 0.05em, upper(name)),
  line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + hair),
))

// Dates and places, quiet and in tabular figures.
#let aside(body) = text(weight: "regular", fill: muted, number-width: "tabular")[#body]

// An entry's title line heads its bullets.
#let entry-head(body) = block(sticky: true, above: head-gap, below: line-gap, body)

// An entry's head is one line of text: the title at the left, and at the
// right the place and dates as one run. It is a paragraph, not a grid: a
// parser that rebuilds a page's columns reads a grid's cells column by
// column, the dates of every entry apart from their titles, and it parts a
// date set alone in a column of its own from its line too.

// Project/general entry — title left, dates right.
#let entry(title, when) = entry-head(par[#title#h(1fr)#aside(when)])

// Work entry — title left, place and dates right.
#let work-entry(company-role, location, when) = entry-head(par[#company-role#h(1fr)#aside[#location#h(1em)#when]])

// A degree: one line, the year after the degree. Not at the right: three
// years stacked at one edge read as a column of their own, apart from their
// schools. The degrees a line apart.
#let degree(body) = block(above: line-gap, below: line-gap, pad(left: 1em, par(body)))

// === HEADER ===
// A letterhead, as the CV's: the name at the left, on the section heads'
// edge; how to reach him at the right, flush with the rules' end, in two
// lines of two, each mark closing its item, and each column right-aligned so
// its marks line up. The two lines stand exactly as tall as the name, by ink:
// Optima reports no usable cap height, so Typst's default edges are the
// ascender line, and the sides are matched by their glyphs' bounds instead.
// The lines keep the default edges, so the items of a line share a baseline;
// the bounds only set the gap between the lines (the name's ink height less
// the first line's ink above its baseline, a line's box, and the second
// line's ink below its baseline) and lift the lines by that last depth, so
// the tops and the feet of the two sides are level.
#context {
  let inked(top, bottom, body) = measure(text(top-edge: top, bottom-edge: bottom, body)).height
  let name = text(size: 22pt, top-edge: "bounds", bottom-edge: "bounds")[Pingfan Hu, Ph.D.]
  let first = ([Greater Melbourne, Australia], [+61 431 251 227])
  let second = ([pingfanhu\@proton.me], [pingfan.org])
  let above = calc.max(..first.map(t => inked("bounds", "baseline", t)))
  let below = calc.max(..second.map(t => inked("baseline", "bounds", t)))
  let gap = measure(name).height - above - measure[Australia].height - below
  grid(
    columns: (1fr, auto),
    align: (left + bottom, right + bottom),
    name,
    pad(bottom: below, grid(
      columns: (auto, auto),
      column-gutter: 1.5em,
      row-gutter: gap,
      align: right,
      [#first.at(0)~#glyph("map-pin")],
      [#first.at(1)~#glyph("phone")],
      [#link("mailto:pingfanhu@proton.me")[#second.at(0)]~#glyph("mail")],
      [#link("https://pingfan.org")[#second.at(1)]~#glyph("compass")],
    )),
  )
}

// the bio: what he is and does, in two lines under the letterhead, after
// the homepage's
#block(above: section-gap, text(hyphenate: false, par(justify: true)[Research data scientist who uses choice models and simulation to study how customers respond to incentives in energy and transportation. Builds survey tools in R and Python and desktop apps in Rust. Australian permanent resident.]))

#section[Education]

#degree[*George Washington University* - _Ph.D., Systems Engineering_, #aside[2026 (GPA 4.0)]]
#degree[*University of Sydney* - _M.P.E., Mechanical Engineering_, #aside[2018]]
#degree[*Pennsylvania State University* - _B.S., Industrial Engineering_, #aside[2015]]

#section[Skills]
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
# the About page's skills as plain text, one group to a line; see the script
source(here::here("resources/scripts/skills.R"))
cat(skills_typst("inline"))
```

```{=typst}
#section[#link("https://pingfan.org/research")[#text(fill: black)[Research Projects]]]

#entry[*EV Smart Charging* - _Sloan-Funded Project of GWU, UC Davis & UC Irvine_][2023 - 2026]

- Designed a national choice experiment for 1,356 EV owners and managed its recruitment budget across Meta and Dynata, using A/B tests to find the most cost-effective approach.
- Built mixed logit models of customer enrollment, finding that EV owners value flexibility and recurring payments most, and predicted uptake for program designs not yet offered.
- Simulated 10,000 EVs against CAISO and NYISO load in 55 time-of-use and enrollment scenarios: managed charging cut CAISO peaks by up to 5.6 GW, and moderate enrollment, not maximum, proved most cost-effective.
- Presented findings to stakeholders at Southern California Edison, PG&E, National Grid, and the Sloan Foundation.
- First-author papers in _Environmental Research Letters_ and _IEEE VPPC_, a third under review; talks at TRB and ASTR.

#entry[*#link("https://surveydown.org")[surveydown]* - _Open-Source Survey Platform of the Helveston Lab at GWU_][2024 - 2026]

- Lead developer of an open-source R package for programmable, reproducible surveys on Quarto, Shiny, and PostgreSQL: 180+ GitHub stars, 11,000+ CRAN downloads.
- Built sdstudio, its Shiny GUI (2,500+ CRAN downloads), and TidyViz, a Python package for survey data.
- First-author paper in _PLOS ONE_; 2nd prize at the GW Open Source Awards; profiled by GW Engineering.
- Communicated the platform in talks at posit::conf, US-RSE, and GW OSCON 2025 and 2026.

#section[Work Experience]

#work-entry[*Alkaline Software* - _Co-Founder & Principal Engineer_][#glyph("map-pin")~Remote][2026 - Present]

- Lead developer of #link("https://emaki.lol")[Emaki], the studio's agentic development environment; deployed 27 releases.
- Built a reusable Rust + GPUI app template for macOS, Windows, and Linux, now the base of three more apps.
- Created the studio's design system (color, type, icons, motion) and the UI and UX of every app.

#work-entry[*George Washington University* - _Graduate Research Assistant_][#glyph("map-pin")~DC, USA][2023 - 2026]

- Teaching assistant for two R analytics courses of 40 students; presented lectures and mentored every project team.
- Built and evaluated Claude Code skills, MCP servers, and hooks for reproducibility; taught in a GW AI workshop.
- Research assistant, FEWS Lab (May - Aug 2023): modeled the Mid-Atlantic freight network's resilience in Python.

#work-entry[*Harsco Rail* - _Software Engineer_][#glyph("map-pin")~SC, USA & Beijing, China][2021 - 2022]

- Led C++ and CAN bus software for rail maintenance machines across the USA and China; delivered 25 releases.
- Stakeholder liaison between customers, US management, and the China team; ran on-site testing.

#work-entry[*GE Appliances* - _Project Engineer_][#glyph("map-pin")~Qingdao, China][2019 - 2020]

- Edison Engineering Development Program: took 500+ components for 9 washer models into production.

#work-entry[*Kurtz Ersa GmbH* - _Assistant Process Engineer (Intern)_][#glyph("map-pin")~Wertheim, Germany][2017]

- Ran a 2-month Design of Experiments on a new soldering technology across 200 PCB samples.

```
